assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral constraints as a propagation mechanism for credit cycles is a foundational macro-finance idea. Kiyotaki-Moore's dynamic amplification and the Bernanke-Gertler financial accelerator framework became the standard way to model credit frictions. It shaped the macro-financial models used after 2008 and the policy analysis built on them.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore (1997) are the clearest originators of the collateral-constraint cycle mechanism. Gertler's contributions run through the financial accelerator and later work on credit frictions in monetary policy models. Gilchrist is an important empirical and quantitative contributor but is left out to keep to three. Bernanke's share of the accelerator was already recognised in 2022, which complicates the attribution but does not erase Gertler's independent contributions.
assessment.maturity: The core papers date from the 1990s and have been confirmed over decades by theoretical extensions, quantitative models, and empirical work on financial crises. Timing is not a concern.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises may lower the priority for some members.
Whether Gertler is better credited here or alongside the New Keynesian monetary policy cluster.
The empirical validation of the mechanism is mixed outside crisis episodes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work changed how economists understand technology, trade exposure and labour demand, and it links closely to wage inequality. The task-based view of technological change and the local labour market evidence on import competition shifted both research and policy debate. It is closely tied to labour economics and uses transparent quasi-experimental designs.
assessment.attribution: Autor is central to both the task framework and the trade-shock evidence. Hanson is co-originator of the China-shock empirical agenda. Katz contributed the earlier supply-demand-and-skill-premium framework that anchors the literature. Dorn is a key co-author on the trade-shock work and is left out only by the three-name limit; the line between him and Katz is a judgment call. Related institutional and technology-direction work already recognised in 2024 and the 2023 labour history prize overlap with the neighbouring territory.
assessment.maturity: The skill-biased technical change literature is decades old, and the China-shock papers have a decade or more of replication, extension and critique.
uncertainties: Debate over the size and persistence of the China-shock effects, and over identification strategies.
Overlap with prior laureates in labour and technology topics.
Difficulty of splitting credit among Autor, Dorn, Hanson and Katz.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data made it possible to measure intergenerational mobility, neighbourhood effects and the causal impact of place at scale, and this redefined empirical work on inequality of opportunity. The research has had large policy influence and set a new standard for data and design in labour and public economics.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the clear intellectual leader. Hendren is closely associated with the causal neighbourhood and childhood exposure estimates, and Friedman with the mobility measurement and tax-record work. Katz is a co-author on the Moving to Opportunity reanalysis but is not proposed here.
assessment.maturity: The central results date from roughly 2014 to the present, so the evidence base is still developing. Replication and follow-up are growing, but the long-run confirmation record is shorter than for older candidates.
uncertainties: Whether the field has had enough time to test the causal neighbourhood estimates.
Dependence on proprietary or restricted administrative data limits independent replication.
Chetty's work spans several topics, so the discovery attribution may be diffuse.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structural estimation of differentiated-product demand with endogenous prices (the BLP approach) and the dynamic industry models from Ericson-Pakes transformed empirical industrial organisation. They became a standard tool in merger review, antitrust and regulation, and across many fields applied to demand.
assessment.attribution: Pakes is the central figure across the demand estimation and dynamic game methods. Berry and Levinsohn are co-authors of the 1995 BLP paper, with Berry also important for the identification results. Others on the list (Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard, Levin) made real contributions in neighbouring areas but are not proposed.
assessment.maturity: The methods are around thirty years old, have been used extensively in practice, and are well confirmed.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as a methods contribution versus a discovery about the economy.
Sensitivity of BLP estimates to implementation and instrument choices.
The boundary of credit between the demand and the dynamic industry strands.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting changed the central unit of analysis in trade from industry to firm. The Melitz model explains reallocation gains from trade, and Helpman's work extends this to the organisation of production and to labour market frictions and inequality. It reshaped both empirical and quantitative work.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the clear originator of the heterogeneous-firm trade model. Helpman has a longer record, from the new trade theory to the heterogeneous-firm extensions. Redding is an important later contributor to quantitative spatial and trade models but is not proposed. The Krugman prize in 2008 covered the earlier trade-and-location wave and does not overlap with this specific contribution.
assessment.maturity: The central models are over twenty years old and have been tested with firm-level data across many countries.
uncertainties: Credit may be contested relative to Bernard, Eaton and Kortum and others outside this ballot's names.
Debate about how much of the gains-from-trade message depends on specific functional form assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mian and Sufi's work uses geographic variation in household balance sheets to show that credit expansions and household leverage drive booms and busts and that debt overhang depresses demand. It shifted macroeconomic thinking about the role of household debt and the origins of the Great Recession.
assessment.attribution: Mian and Sufi are the joint and clearly identified originators of this agenda, with a long, tightly co-authored body of work. Campbell is a major figure in household finance and asset pricing but is not a natural co-recipient for this specific discovery.
assessment.maturity: The main papers date from about 2009 to 2015 and the research programme is well cited. The long-run evidence is still accumulating, and some findings have been challenged.
uncertainties: Challenges to the empirical interpretation of the credit supply and household demand channels.
Relative recency compared with older candidates.
Overlap with the 2022 prize on financial crises.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantile regression made it possible to study the whole conditional distribution rather than the mean, and it is widely used in labour economics (wage distributions, returns to schooling), finance and policy evaluation. It is a durable methodological contribution with broad reach across the field.
assessment.attribution: Koenker and Bassett (1978) introduced the estimator, and Koenker developed the theory, inference, and software over decades. Chernozhukov made major later contributions on inference and on instrumental variable quantile methods but is also credited under other candidates, so he is not proposed here.
assessment.maturity: The estimator is over forty-five years old and has proven value in practice.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views a single estimator as sufficient for the prize.
Relative standing of econometric methods versus applied discoveries in the current pool, and overlap with earlier econometrics prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-run tax-record series on top incomes and wealth built a new empirical foundation for the study of inequality and informed a large public and academic debate. The data discovery and the offshore wealth estimates matter, and they have influenced tax policy debates. Under the criterion of data discovery combined with an explanatory framework, the framework side is more contested than the measurement side.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez are the originators of the top income series, and Zucman is the lead on offshore wealth and on distributional national accounts. The distinction between the measurement contribution and the theoretical claims (for example about r > g) matters for credit. Saez also appears under another candidate in the optimal taxation cluster.
assessment.maturity: The top income work dates from the early 2000s and has been extended to many countries. Some of the later wealth and distributional estimates are still debated.
uncertainties: Methodological critiques of the wealth and distributional estimates.
The extent to which the prize would reward measurement versus a tested explanatory framework.
Possible concern about policy advocacy alongside the scientific work, which the criteria say should not weigh on the decision.
